rationale: The exact submitted lifecycle claim is contradicted by its byte-verified source. The full retained text (characters 0-850) and operative span (390-849) direct flags at the White House and public buildings in the District of Columbia and Illinois to be at half mast on the funeral day, expressly Wednesday, August 22, 1934. August 21, 1934 appears in the signature block. The card instead assigns August 21 as both the clause first_end and whole_order_end, and repeatedly misstates the commanded calendar day as August 21. A signature date does not end a command expressly applicable the following day. The direct whole-command calendar limitation supports own-terms expiration at the end of August 22 on this retained text, without needing proof of performance; it cannot support the submitted August 21 expiration. This is a substantive date error, not a source-byte mismatch. The inventory otherwise contains the one complete flag command; the commemorative recital, signature and order number create no additional independent command. The retained text contains no savings clause or surviving independent duty. It supplies no earlier ending event. Thus the exact ending date and related reasoning fail even though the general conclusion that this one-day command is no longer operative is supported on the retained representation. No replacement claim, original authentication, or human certification is issued.
